candidates.name: MTA-Ridership-Data-Analysis-Dashboard
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed MTA_Daily_Ridership.xlsx snapshot of the MTA's official 'Daily Ridership Data: Beginning 2020' dataset, covering subway, bus, LIRR, Metro-North, Access-A-Ride, bridges & tunnels traffic, and Staten Island Railway from 2020 onward, plus a dashboard build.
candidates.why_useful: Multi-modal NYC transit ridership recovery/level series can act as a local visitor-and-mobility proxy for one of ABNB's largest single markets (gap 10, transit as visitor proxy); a static committed copy avoids relying on the live Socrata endpoint.
candidates.size_hint: single xlsx, multi-sheet, daily rows across ~7 modes

candidates.name: mta-ridership-map
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed CSVs (Stations.csv, ridership.csv, joined.csv) plus nyc.json geodata and pull/join scripts mapping NYC MTA subway ridership to station locations.
candidates.why_useful: Station-level subway ridership panel usable as a granular NYC tourist-corridor mobility proxy (e.g., airport-linked or Manhattan-core stations) rather than only system-wide totals.
candidates.time_coverage: not stated in README (older snapshot, repo dormant since 2022)

candidates.name: NY-MetroMetrics
candidates.what_it_holds: Data-engineering/ETL pipeline (Apache-2.0) that extracts MTA ridership data (subway, bus, Metro-North) for post-pandemic analysis; no data files confirmed committed, README does not specify exact source files or date range.
candidates.why_useful: Reusable extraction pipeline for the official MTA ridership feeds if a point-in-time pull is needed, but contributes no new dataset itself.
candidates.size_hint: pipeline code, no confirmed data size

candidates.name: mta-ridership
candidates.what_it_holds: Jupyter notebook (MTA_ridership_01-03-22.ipynb) plus Resources/Images analyzing MTA subway, bus, and vehicular (bridge/tunnel) ridership from March 2020 to March 2021.
candidates.why_useful: Narrow COVID-window ridership analysis; marginal value as it predates the demand regime relevant to the 2026 pitch and is a single narrow snapshot.

candidates.name: msp_dal_backtest
candidates.what_it_holds: data/msp_passengers.csv: monthly MSP airport enplanement counts 2015-2024 (~120 obs) sourced from Metropolitan Airports Commission monthly operations reports, paired with data/dal_prices.csv (Tiingo monthly DAL closes); backtest code testing MSP passenger momentum as a leading signal for Delta Air Lines equity, with COVID period excluded and optional seasonal adjustment.
candidates.why_useful: Directly analogous 'book-ahead volume as equity signal' methodology (kernel analogue per gap 18, cruise/airline advance-volume-as-signal) and a concrete airport-enplanement time series/pull method that could be replicated for airports feeding ABNB-heavy markets.

candidates.name: hkimmd-scrapper
candidates.what_it_holds: Scraper (Apache-2.0) targeting immd.gov.hk (Hong Kong Immigration Department) for airport/border passenger-traffic statistics — a working, non-Airbnb-site method for pulling Hong Kong visitor-arrival counts.
candidates.why_useful: Working scraper for an official APAC border-crossing/airport arrivals source not already in our government-data holdings; relevant to regional travel volume in Asia (gap 7) via a rail/airport-link proxy.
candidates.time_coverage: whatever immd.gov.hk currently publishes (scraper, not a static archive)

candidates.name: LAX-Dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: CSV recovered from data.gov's 'Los Angeles International Airport Passenger Traffic By Terminal' dataset, a static single-airport terminal-level passenger count file.
candidates.why_useful: Terminal-level LAX passenger traffic could proxy inbound visitor volume to the LA market (one of the 13 Inside Airbnb panel cities), though it is a single static pull of a government dataset we could fetch directly.

candidates.name: ratp-open-datas
candidates.what_it_holds: Script that downloads a fresh copy of RATP (Paris metro/RER operator) Open Data and builds per-station JSON files; no ridership counts confirmed, appears focused on station/line metadata rather than passenger volumes.
candidates.why_useful: Could be adapted to pull RATP station-level data if RATP publishes ridership counts in its open-data portal, relevant to Paris (an Inside Airbnb panel city) visitor-proxy work.

candidates.name: hacking-the-paris-subway
candidates.what_it_holds: Prediction/optimization project for Paris subway (RATP) schedules using RATP open data; primarily a scheduling-optimization exercise, ridership-data content unconfirmed from README alone.
candidates.why_useful: Possible secondary pointer to RATP open-data ridership tables if inspected further, but as listed it reads as a scheduling project rather than a ridership archive.

candidates.name: transport-for-paris-france
candidates.what_it_holds: Contains no ridership data — an API-Evangelist bulk-registered profile repo holding only an apis.yml machine-readable pointer to the RATP Open Data API surface (confirmed via file listing: kin/, screenshots/, security/, README.md, apis.yml). No OpenAPI spec or data files present.
candidates.why_useful: Only useful as a discovery pointer to RATP's own open-data API; contributes no data itself.

candidates.name: airports-by-passenger-traffic-ETL
candidates.what_it_holds: A simple ETL pipeline described as processing 'airports passenger traffic' data; source and geographic scope not detailed in the search listing.
candidates.why_useful: Potential reusable ETL pattern for airport passenger-traffic ingestion if the underlying source (unconfirmed) is a usable public feed; needs closer inspection before relying on it.

candidates.name: airports-project
candidates.what_it_holds: Two Excel files with a brief analysis of airport passenger traffic in India (scope/years not detailed beyond the description).
candidates.why_useful: Possible small India airport-traffic dataset relevant to APAC regional travel-volume gap, though scope looks thin (described as 'brief analysis').

candidates.name: MetisMTAProject
candidates.what_it_holds: Links MTA ridership data, subway station locations, and hospital locations (older Metis bootcamp project, 2020) to identify underserved areas; ridership data likely pulled from MTA turnstile data, not health/tourism focused.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal — the underserved-areas health framing is off-thesis, but the underlying MTA turnstile-to-station join logic could be repurposed for a station-level tourist-corridor cut.

queries_run: gh search repos "mta ridership data" --sort stars
gh search repos "tfl ridership OR tfl open data" --sort stars
gh search repos "RATP open data" --sort stars
gh search repos "airport passenger traffic" --sort stars
gh search repos "NYC TLC airport taxi trips" --sort stars
gh search repos "japan railway passengers OR JR ridership OR narita passengers" --sort stars
WebFetch raw READMEs and gh api contents listings for shortlisted repos
notes: Dead ends: TfL-specific search returned zero results (no repo description matched 'tfl ridership' or 'tfl open data' text directly — TfL's own open-data API is well known but GitHub mirrors of TfL ridership counts did not surface; a follow-up scout could try 'tfl.gov.uk open data', 'oyster card data', or 'London Underground station usage' as more specific terms). NYC TLC airport-taxi-trip search and Japan rail/airport passenger searches both returned zero repos — worth retrying with terms like 'nyc taxi trip data github', 'JR East IR passenger statistics', 'Haneda Narita monthly passengers', or checking JNTO/Japan-government open-data portals directly rather than GitHub search, since Japanese rail/airport operators do not appear to have GitHub-native ridership mirrors. WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-session (this session had already used 200/200 web searches from prior work), so I relied on WebFetch (unmetered) for repo README/content inspection instead — a few promising leads (RATP ridership specifically, JR/Narita/Haneda passenger data, London Underoriginal station-level Oyster/contactless counts) were not fully chased down via WebSearch and are worth a dedicated re-scout. Most MTA-themed repos found are small student/bootcamp analyses of the same official MTA 'Daily Ridership Data: Beginning 2020' Socrata dataset (2020-present only, no pre-2020 archive found) — none add a materially longer or point-in-time version of what a human could pull directly from MTA's own open-data portal, so ratings are capped at medium. The MSP-DAL backtest repo is the most conceptually interesting find: it operationalizes airport enplanements as a leading equity signal, which is the same 'book-ahead volume as kernel proxy' logic as gap #18 (cruise advance sales) and could be replicated for airports serving ABNB-heavy markets (e.g., a Paris CDG/Orly, Barcelona, or Sydney enplanement series) if such committed CSVs exist on GitHub — worth a targeted follow-up search on '<city> airport passengers csv github' for the 13-city Inside Airbnb panel.
